The adoption of LLMs has become increasingly prominent in scientific writing and analyses because of the availability of free applications such as ChatGPT.

In addition to generating code, LLMs can also assist with the following routine coding activities (see also Lubiana et al., 2023). Explain code (to yourself and others): It is not uncommon to have code or code snippets that you did not write (e.g. imported or modified from a paper, a collaborator, GitHub or Stack Overflow) or code that you wrote in the past and did not document well.

We know that not every author reads all the code associated with a paper, but at least one author must do so, and take responsibility for it. Using an LLM to help generate the code does not change this fact. When using an LLM, we would expect the responsible author(s) to follow the same kinds of quality assurance checks as they would if the code was written by them independently.
